subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool-capability descriptor taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy, audit, inventory, and Gateway consumers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines public SDK/Gateway security-policy facts and overlaps with provenance, default-deny permissions, Security Matrix, and manifest egress-intent work that automation cannot reconcile safely.

options.title: Approve Unified Descriptor Contract
options.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventories, Gateway schemas, and hook/trusted-policy events, and document that declarations never bypass host policy.

options.title: Fold Into Capability Permissions
options.body: Keep this issue blocked behind the broader default-deny capability permission model so descriptors ship only as part of an enforceable grant subsystem.

options.title: Limit To Security Matrix First
options.body: Use the Security Matrix or audit model as the first consumer and defer a general public descriptor field until that vocabulary lands.

recommendation.title: Approve Unified Descriptor Contract
recommendation.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventories, Gateway schemas, and hook/trusted-policy events, and document that declarations never bypass host policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Their host-hook contract work is the closest existing SDK seam for a public trusted-policy and tool-metadata facts decision.
